attributes.axis_log: REVERIFY of attempt.updatefxstreak-exact-drive-w2 first: baseline re-derived as real 134, insns 138/138, opcode multiset IDENTICAL - matches the record exactly, so its four dead axes stand and were not re-run. AXIS 5 (new) explicit value identity for the shared operands: introduced f32 vx/vy/vz and sx/sy/sz holding e->vel[0..2] and pos[0..2] at their existing point of use, and rewrote the six p0/p1 fmadd expressions to read the locals, making the sharing the prior pass said was load-bearing EXPLICIT in the source instead of leaving it to CSE. REGRESSED real 134 -> 144, insns still 138/138. CAUSE READ FROM --ops, not inferred: the target has MORE memory traffic than we do, not less - the cluster shows target-only ['lfs','fmul','stfs'] at T[94:97] and target-only ['lfs','frsp','fmadd'] at T[105:108], while ours gains paired frsp. So the target RE-READS e->vel[]/pos[] inside the quad block rather than holding them, and caching them in named f32 locals both removes the reloads the target performs and forces extra rounding on the f64 fwd multiply. This inverts the premise of the prior pass's AXIS 2 post-mortem ('separating the blocks breaks the vel[]/pos[] load sharing'): the blocks are not sharing loads in the target at all at those sites, so no caching form can rescue that reorder. Reverted; no source change retained.

attributes.residual: 134 lines, unchanged, ONE named mechanism, and this pass sharpened its description. Structure remains exact: opcode multiset IDENTICAL 138/138, frame 0x1C0, _savefpr_28, all 12 quad stores and both NormalVector calls byte-exact. The residual is (a) a volatile-FPR renaming seeded at the first instruction after the prologue (target loads the first f64 constant into f2 and gClockTime into f0; ours uses f0 and f1) which rotates four registers through the entry block despite byte-identical instruction ORDER, and (b) the 28-instruction reorder window at 0x150-0x1bc where target interleaves quad[0..2] between the p0 and p1 fmadds. NEW THIS PASS: the reorder window is NOT enabled by operand caching - the target re-reads vel/pos there (extra lfs on the target side), so the interleave is a pure scheduler choice over rematerialized loads, and the source-side lever space for it is empty. Five distinct axes are now dead across two passes. NOT WEBFRANK-READY, unchanged and re-confirmed: this is a permutation PLUS a register rotation, so permute_instruction_atoms' dependence audit runs on our pre-recolour image where the target's interleave is only legal under target's FPR assignment. Do not flag it.
